subject.title: Dashboard: shared vs private tabs + role/scope-gated visibility

question: Should shared/private dashboard tabs be a hard authorization boundary in the dashboard store, or only a UI organization/filtering feature?
rationale: The request crosses Control UI, operator scopes, privacy expectations, and persistent dashboard state; automation cannot decide what security promise `visibility` or `scope` should make.

options.title: Define Store-Enforced Visibility
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved model where private tabs are filtered at store/API boundaries and the UI only reflects that enforced result.

options.title: Scope To UX Filtering
options.body: Treat shared/private as an organizational UI hint with explicit documentation that it is not a strong separation boundary.

options.title: Defer Bundled Multi-User Semantics
options.body: Leave the dashboard stack without tab privacy until the broader multi-operator model is settled or moved to an external plugin path.

recommendation.title: Define Store-Enforced Visibility
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved model where private tabs are filtered at store/API boundaries and the UI only reflects that enforced result.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal is the recently merged plugin-tab seam and Logbook precedent that this dashboard roadmap builds on.
